userStories.title: The thread link table and its repository
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the thread-only link between ApprovalRequest and assistant provenance, with a transactional repository.

**Motivation** — `PendingAction` duplicates what `ApprovalRequest` now models (actor, on-behalf-of, mode, approver, status, result, expiry), and opens a second record, an `assistant_action` `FleetApproval`, so the fleet inbox can show it.

**Approach** — Migration `20261105090000_assistant_action_request`. `ApprovalRequest` gains `assistantAction AssistantActionRequest?` and `ChatThread` gains `assistantActionRequests AssistantActionRequest[]`.

`src/fleet/assistant/requests/assistant-action-request.domain.ts` holds `ASSISTANT_ACTION_REQUEST_REPOSITORY`, the record types and `MAX_PENDING_ACTIONS = 10` (from US-001 on, the import every reader uses). `PrismaAssistantActionRequestRepository` (same directory):
- `insert(link)`: one row; answers it.
- `findByRequest(requestId)`: the row or null.
- `lockThread(threadId)`: `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on the `ChatThread` row; false when it is gone (the same query as `PrismaPendingActionRepository.lockThread`).
- `lockByRequest(requestId)`: `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on the link row; null when gone.
- `insertSystemNote(threadId, content)`: one `system` message with the next `seq` from `allocateThreadSeq`; answers its id (the same write as `PrismaPendingActionRepository.insertSystemNote`).
- `markNoted(requestId, noteMessageId, at)`.
- `countPendingInThread(threadId)`: rows of the thread whose request status is `pending`.
- `findScopedInThread(requestId, projectId, threadId)`: the row with its request when the row's thread is `threadId` and the request's project is `projectId`, else null.
- `findOwnRequest(requestId, projectId, actor)`: the `ApprovalRequest` whose id and project match and whose `actorType`/`actorId` are the actor's, with its link when one exists, else null.

**The thread link is its own table, not columns on `ApprovalRequest`.** `AssistantActionRequest` (one row per thread request, keyed by `requestId`) holds the thread, job, tool call, tool name, preview and the note and delivery marks. These are thread bookkeeping, not approval state, and the engine stays free of thread knowledge. An MCP request gets no link row.

**Scope** — In: add only the new Prisma model/relations, its migration, domain types, AbstractPrismaRepository implementation and private token/useExisting registration in AssistantModule; add the repository integration spec. Reuse transaction-scoped Prisma access and the existing sequence allocator. Out: command registration (US-002), outcome subscriber (US-003), executor/read switching (US-005 onward), and dropping PendingAction (US-011). Pending `PendingAction` rows are not migrated (design decision 2); the drop discards them. A pending request whose thread is deleted keeps its `ApprovalRequest` (only the link cascades); it can still be decided or expire. Deciding does not check `threadsEnabled` (the engine's decide route has no thread knowledge).

**Interface** —
```prisma
model AssistantActionRequest {
  requestId          String    @id
  threadId           String?
  jobId              String?
  toolCallId         String?
  tool               String
  preview            String    @db.Text
  noteMessageId      String?
  notedAt            DateTime?
  deliveredAt        DateTime?
  deliveredMessageId String?
  createdAt          DateTime  @default(now())

  request ApprovalRequest @relation(fields: [requestId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  thread  ChatThread?     @relation(fields: [threadId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([threadId])
  @@index([threadId, deliveredAt])
  @@index([deliveredMessageId])
}
```

Verification: regenerate Prisma with `bun run db:generate` from the repo root. Run the repository's DB-backed specs outside the sandbox, including migration-backed setup; API type-check remains a verification step, not an acceptance criterion.

userStories.title: Outcome notes from request events
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Write exactly one terminal outcome note per linked request through the approval outbox subscriber.

**Motivation** — `PendingAction` duplicates what `ApprovalRequest` now models (actor, on-behalf-of, mode, approver, status, result, expiry), and opens a second record, an `assistant_action` `FleetApproval`, so the fleet inbox can show it.

**Approach** — `requestOutcomeNote({ requestId, tool, status, result })` answers, with `<text>` capped at `NOTE_RESULT_MAX` (500) characters plus `…`:

| Request status | Result | Note |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `executed` | `{ text }` | `Action <id> (<tool>) was approved and done: <text>` |
| `failed` | `name` `NotFoundAppException` | `Action <id> (<tool>) was approved but failed: not_found` |
| `failed` | any other | `Action <id> (<tool>) was approved but failed: error: <tool> failed` |
| `rejected` | — | `Action <id> (<tool>) was rejected.` |
| `expired` | — | `Action <id> (<tool>) expired without a decision.` |
| `cancelled` | — | `Action <id> (<tool>) was cancelled.` |

`AssistantActionOutcomeSubscriber` (registered on `FanOutPublisher` for `APPROVAL_REQUEST_CHANGED`; `AssistantModule` imports `OutboxCoreModule` for it) handles a payload whose status is one of those five:
1. No link for `requestId`, or a link with no `threadId`: nothing.
2. In one transaction: `lockThread(threadId)` (false: nothing), `lockByRequest(requestId)`, and if `notedAt` is set, nothing. Otherwise read the request (`ApprovalRequestQueries.findById`), insert the system note and `markNoted`.
3. After the commit: a `message` frame with the note's id and a `thread` frame on `ThreadEventBus`.

Any other status is ignored. A malformed payload is skipped with a `warn`.

**Outcome notes are written by an outbox subscriber.** `approval_request_changed` is recorded in the transaction that changed the status, and the relay retries a failed handler. So the note is written once, after the change commits, however the request was settled (decided, executed, swept, cancelled). The note can appear one relay interval after the decision. The subscriber declares `@SystemWriter('system.thread.ingest')`, the key of the other system writer of thread transcript rows (`ThreadIngestHook`), and runs in the relay's own `runAsSystem('outbox')` context (an allowlisted unaudited surface); it does not open `runAsSystemWriter`.

**Scope** — In: request-outcome-note helper/unit tests, subscriber/integration tests, AssistantModule OutboxCoreModule import and subscriber provider, and the system-writer map entry `[AssistantActionOutcomeSubscriber, 'system.thread.ingest']` with expected count 36 -> 37 and unchanged declared key set. Allow DB failures to reach fan-out/relay retries; only malformed/no-link/nonterminal/deleted-thread cases are no-ops. Out: delivering notes to the next agent turn (US-004), opening requests (US-005), and route-driven decision/failure/expiry coverage (US-008). An approved command that fails does not carry the tool's own failure sentence to the agent; the note names `not_found` or `error: <tool> failed`, and the request's `result` holds the error name. US-008 only: an outcome note lags the decision by one outbox relay interval.

**Interface** — `requestOutcomeNote({ requestId, tool, status, result })`; `AssistantActionOutcomeSubscriber` registers for `APPROVAL_REQUEST_CHANGED` in module init and declares `@SystemWriter('system.thread.ingest')`. Read canonical request state through `ApprovalRequestQueries.findById`; keep noteMessageId/notedAt on the link, not on ApprovalRequest.

userStories.title: Outcome delivery from requests
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Deliver terminal linked-request outcomes to the agent once and reconstruct the same handoff on every job assignment.

**Motivation** — `PendingAction` duplicates what `ApprovalRequest` now models (actor, on-behalf-of, mode, approver, status, result, expiry), and opens a second record, an `assistant_action` `FleetApproval`, so the fleet inbox can show it.

**Approach** — Delivery reads the link and request tables instead of `PendingAction`:
- `PrismaChatThreadRepository.deliverOutcomeNotes(threadId, messageId, userText)`: the thread's links whose request status is one of the five and whose `deliveredAt` is null, oldest first, at most `MAX_DELIVERED_NOTES`; notes from `requestOutcomeNote`; `deliveryText`; the first `delivered` marked with `deliveredAt` and `deliveredMessageId`.
- `PrismaFleetJobRepository.initialMessageText(message)`: the links delivered on `message.id`, rebuilt the same way.

`DELIVERABLE_STATUSES` becomes the five lowercase request statuses.

The five statuses are `executed`, `failed`, `rejected`, `expired` and `cancelled`. Derive notes using the US-003 helper, not by reading transcript system messages; notes may not have been written by the relay yet. Preserve existing deliveryText UTF-8 byte limits, header, user-text suffix, first-fitting-prefix behavior, MAX_DELIVERED_NOTES and deterministic creation order. Mark only the prefix actually handed over and keep repeated assignments read-only. The existing sendMessage return is { message, jobId, deduplicated }, not a handoff-text DTO: message.content stays the plain user input. For live-session delivery assertions, observe the persisted THREAD_INPUT command's payload.text; for new-turn delivery, use a separate new-turn fixture and observe findThreadAssign(...).initialMessage.text. Do not add a return field or prepend outcome notes to stored user message content.

**Scope** — In: outcome-delivery.ts/status assertion, the two repository delivery reads/marks, new assistant-request-delivery integration tests, and replacement fixtures in prisma-chat-thread.repository.spec.ts, prisma-fleet-job.repository.find-thread-assign.spec.ts, assistant-action-delivery.integration.spec.ts and assistant-action-send-delivery.integration.spec.ts. Preserve their once-only send and repeatable assign invariants while seeding requests/links instead of PendingAction or AssistantActionService. Out: the event subscriber/helper already delivered by US-003, pendingActions detail query (US-007), executor gating (US-005/006/009), and dropping old storage/helper files (US-011).

**Interface** — `PrismaChatThreadRepository.deliverOutcomeNotes(threadId, messageId, userText)`; `PrismaFleetJobRepository.initialMessageText(message)`; `DELIVERABLE_STATUSES = ['executed', 'failed', 'rejected', 'expired', 'cancelled']`. The public send/assignment DTOs and deliveryText contract remain unchanged.

AC-7 [integration] A second findThreadAssign for the same job returns the same initialMessage.text.

userStories.title: Waiting thread writes through the gate
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Resolve assistant policy and open waiting thread writes through ApprovalGate with a capped, transactional thread link and scoped action reads.

**Motivation** — `approvalModeFor` (`src/fleet/assistant/actions/approval-policy.ts`) is a code default: a user's thread write waits for the user, everything else runs at once. Nothing reads a policy, so koda #301 ("configurable approval policy per tool") is still open.

**Approach** — `AssistantToolExecutor.writeTool`, for an origin of kind `thread`, after the permission check and the preview (both unchanged):
1. `mode = (await resolver.resolve({ key: tool.key, projectId, subject: { type: 'ASSISTANT', id: 'assistant' } })).mode`.
2. **Any mode but `none`:** in one transaction: `lockThread(threadId)` (false answers `not_found`); `countPendingInThread(threadId) >= MAX_PENDING_ACTIONS` answers `refused: 10 actions are pending in this thread; wait for the user to decide them` with outcome `refused`; otherwise the gate opens or answers the pending request, and the link (`requestId`, `threadId`, `jobId`, `toolCallId`, the tool's name, the preview) is inserted unless one exists for that request, inside `bookkeeping('assistant.action-request-link', ...)`. The call answers `pending <requestId>: awaiting approval; do not retry`, outcome `pending`. After the commit, one `thread` frame is published on `ThreadEventBus` for a newly linked request.
3. A throw from the gate or the transaction is caught outside the transaction and answers `error: <tool> failed`, with the stack logged.
4. **`none`:** in US-005 the existing `directWrite` still runs (it records a `PendingAction` through `recordDirect`); US-006 replaces it.

`koda_get_action` in a thread reads `findScopedInThread(id, ctx.projectId, ctx.threadId)` from US-005 on. Its lines: `action <id> <tool> <status>`, `requested <createdAt>`, `decided <decidedAt>` when set, `settled <settledAt>` when set, then `result:` and the fenced result `text` when the request has one. `ActionTools` injects both the link repository and `PENDING_ACTION_REPOSITORY` until US-009 moves the MCP read; from US-009 on it injects only the link repository.

The context is the one `executeUnstored` already opens (`SYSTEM/assistant`, on behalf of the requester, origin `thread`), so the gate's subject is `ASSISTANT`.

**The mode is resolved before any lock.** The executor asks `ApprovalPolicyResolver.resolve` (newly exported by `ApprovalEngineModule`) for the call's mode first. A `none` write calls the gate with no transaction and no lock, so the tool runs exactly as the direct path ran it before: its writes are its own, a batch tool's partial writes stand, and no thread lock is held while a fleet tool takes a job lock (the ingest fold and job effects lock job, then thread). A waiting write takes the thread lock, checks the cap, opens the request through the gate and writes the link in one transaction that runs no tool. The one exception is a policy that changes between the executor's resolution and the gate's: a write resolved as waiting that the gate runs at once runs its tool inside that transaction.

The preceding none-path gate behavior is the US-006 integration; this story deliberately retains directWrite for that branch until then. A gate outcome of executed after a waiting-to-none policy change returns the executed result and does not fabricate a pending request or link.

**The cap is checked before the gate's duplicate lookup.** With 10 linked requests pending, a retry of a pending write with a new `toolCallId` is refused rather than answered with the existing request id. The agent is told not to retry a pending write. The gate's duplicate key includes the input's `jobId`, so the same write asked in a new turn opens a second request, bounded by the cap.

**An agent-created thread's write now waits.** The gate treats every assistant call as subject `ASSISTANT`, whose default is `human`, whether the requester is a user or an agent. Before this feature an agent's thread write ran at once. The agent (the on-behalf-of principal) may approve it with `koda_decide_approval`, and an admin can set an `ASSISTANT` policy of `none`.

**Scope** — In: export ApprovalPolicyResolver from ApprovalEngineModule; inject gate, resolver, ASSISTANT_ACTION_REQUEST_REPOSITORY, ThreadEventBus and TRANSACTION_MANAGER into the executor; replace its waiting thread branch; switch thread koda_get_action reads; add bookkeeping reason assistant.action-request-link with text "The thread link of a waiting assistant write: its thread, job, tool call, tool and preview; the request is `approval.request-open`." and pin EXPECTED_REASON_IDS. Keep permission, preview refusal and replay behavior unchanged. Add assistant-thread-gate integration tests and update executor.spec.ts, executor.agent-caller.spec.ts, write-tool-errors.spec.ts and tools/action-tools.spec.ts.

Replace old proposal/approval fixtures in assistant-action-actor (only its two thread-request actor cases here), assistant-action-tools, assistant-actor-approve, assistant-add-memory-tool, assistant-cancel-job-tool, assistant-create-tickets-tool, assistant-dispatch-job-tool, assistant-link-tickets-tool, assistant-record-decision-tool, assistant-requeue-job-tool, assistant-update-ticket-tool and permissions-assistant-tools integration specs. Approve through POST /approvals/:id/decisions; assert ApprovalRequest/link instead of PendingAction, lowercase status and requester authorship. Approved tool failures assert result error name, and approved partial batches assert full rollback rather than partial text/writes. Delete assistant-actions-propose.integration.spec.ts. Remove audit-fleet-assistant-actions cases for the old decide/expire keys and assert request opening is bookkeeping; remove only the obsolete S5b assistant_action decide block from endpoint.e2e.spec.ts.

Out: replacing direct thread writes (US-006), pendingActions detail and widened deciding coverage (US-007), asynchronous outcomes (US-008), MCP gating/read removal (US-009), and deleting PendingAction code (US-011). The fleet approvals inbox stops showing assistant actions: no `assistant_action` approval is opened after US-005. The web inbox's assistant panel stays in the code until `permissions-p3-web`, which lists `ApprovalRequest`s in the unified inbox. US-005 only: two concurrent waiting writes of one thread are serialised by the thread row lock, so they cannot both take the last cap slot; the concurrent race itself is not tested here (the lock is the 2a-D4 one, whose concurrency test is deleted with the propose service). Notifying the thread's requester of a new assistant request is not added: the thread card and the live `thread` frame show it, and approval-api's notification goes to users holding `approval.decide`.

**Interface** — `gate(tool.key, { projectId, threadId, jobId, args }, { projectId })`; `findScopedInThread(id, ctx.projectId, ctx.threadId)`; `bookkeeping('assistant.action-request-link', ...)`. The pending tool result is `pending <requestId>: awaiting approval; do not retry`, with outcome pending and isError false.

AC-2 [integration] That call adds no comment.
AC-3 [integration] That call answers content 'pending <requestId>: awaiting approval; do not retry' with isError false.

userStories.title: Decided thread requests: notes, failures and expiry
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Integrate real thread decisions, command failures and engine expiry with relay-driven terminal notes, including approved-batch rollback.

**Motivation** — The design (§4) replaces `PendingAction` and `FleetApproval` with one request model and makes the assistant's tool executors registry entries, so REST (feature 5), MCP and threads share one mechanism.

**Approach** — Deciding is the engine's `POST /approvals/:id/decisions` (approval-api), unchanged. US-007 pins who may decide and what an approve or reject writes; US-008 pins the notes, the failure outcomes and expiry through the relay and the engine's sweeper.

**An approved command's failure fails the request, rolls back, and keeps no tool text.** `ApprovalExecutionService` runs the command inside its settle transaction, and this transaction manager rolls back the outer transaction when any nested `run()` throws, even if the throw is caught (`PrismaTransactionManager`, SEC-16). So the command rethrows every tool error: `NotFoundAppException`, `ToolActionError` and anything else. The engine settles the request `failed` with `result: { error: 'execution-failed', name }`, and none of the tool's writes persist. On the approved path a batch is all-or-nothing, and the agent's note says `not_found` or `error: <tool> failed`; the tool's own failure sentence (2b1-D2, for example `KODA-1 cannot move from CLOSED to IN_PROGRESS`) is not carried. On the direct path the tool's text still reaches the agent.

Outcome-note contract from US-003: `requestOutcomeNote({ requestId, tool, status, result })` answers, with `<text>` capped at `NOTE_RESULT_MAX` (500) characters plus `…`:

| Request status | Result | Note |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `executed` | `{ text }` | `Action <id> (<tool>) was approved and done: <text>` |
| `failed` | `name` `NotFoundAppException` | `Action <id> (<tool>) was approved but failed: not_found` |
| `failed` | any other | `Action <id> (<tool>) was approved but failed: error: <tool> failed` |
| `rejected` | — | `Action <id> (<tool>) was rejected.` |
| `expired` | — | `Action <id> (<tool>) expired without a decision.` |
| `cancelled` | — | `Action <id> (<tool>) was cancelled.` |

**Outcome notes are written by an outbox subscriber.** `approval_request_changed` is recorded in the transaction that changed the status, and the relay retries a failed handler. So the note is written once, after the change commits, however the request was settled (decided, executed, swept, cancelled). The note can appear one relay interval after the decision. The subscriber declares `@SystemWriter('system.thread.ingest')`, the key of the other system writer of thread transcript rows (`ThreadIngestHook`), and runs in the relay's own `runAsSystem('outbox')` context (an allowlisted unaudited surface); it does not open `runAsSystemWriter`.

Drive real requests opened by the thread route, approve/reject through POST /api/approvals/:id/decisions, then explicitly dispatch OutboxRelay.dispatchPendingBatch before checking transcript notes. Soft-delete a pending comment's ticket to exercise NotFoundAppException. For koda_link_tickets, propose links to SB-1/SB-2 and soft-delete SB-2 before approval; confirm failure and absence of the earlier SB-1 link. Use the real ApprovalRequestExpirySweeper.tick after expiresAt; obtain this provided-but-not-exported provider with app.get(ApprovalRequestExpirySweeper, { strict: false }).

**Scope** — In: author assistant-thread-outcomes.integration.spec.ts for the declared decision/subscriber/engine seam and delete assistant-actions-expiry.integration.spec.ts, which pins the removed legacy sweeper. This integration-focused story is an explicit binding spec slice; do not merge it or create a separate validation story. Production behavior comes from US-002/003/005/007 and the existing engine. Out: rebuilding the engine, changing its decide/expiry routes, authoring a second note writer, direct-path partial-write changes (US-006), and deleting the legacy sweeper implementation (US-011). An approved command that fails does not carry the tool's own failure sentence to the agent; the note names `not_found` or `error: <tool> failed`, and the request's `result` holds the error name. US-008 only: an outcome note lags the decision by one outbox relay interval.

**Interface** — `ApprovalRequestExpirySweeper.tick`; `OutboxRelay.dispatchPendingBatch`; `POST /approvals/:id/decisions`; failed execution result `result: { error: 'execution-failed', name }`. Do not weaken real-DB rollback assertions or count sandbox skips as verification.

analysis:
Goal and baseline: close #301 by moving the nine assistant write tools, in threads and over MCP, onto the already implemented P3 approval engine. This is an existing-code migration, not a second approval engine or a new policy API. The supplied source-root framework detection is inaccurate: the API uses NestJS/Fastify and Nathapp platform modules, and the web uses Nuxt/Vue, not Express/Next.js (.nax/mono/apps/api/context.md:25; .nax/mono/apps/web/context.md:24). The feature spec is committed at .nax/features/permissions-p3-approval-assistant/spec.md:1. Codebase-memory MCP is not exposed in this session; structural discovery therefore used direct reads and text searches against the supplied execution root. No code or tests were executed during PRD drafting. The nathapp-nestjs-patterns skill is also not exposed among the available tools/files; implementation agents must load it if available before writing NestJS code. Do not edit generated AGENTS.md or .nax/mono context files.

Existing engine and integration seams: apps/api/src/approvals/approval-command.registry.ts:15 defines ApprovalCommand with key, parse, execute and optional toResult; parse must accept its own JSON-serialisable output. Registration rejects non-approvable and duplicate keys (same file:33). AssistantToolRegistry.list() already exposes registration order (apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/assistant-tool.registry.ts:25). AssistantModule already imports ApprovalEngineModule, but its providers still include the old proposal service, decisions handler, repository and expiry sweeper (apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/assistant.module.ts:43,67,86). Add AssistantToolCommands after the synchronous tool-group registrations and prove the actual module.init() seam in its DB-free module spec. Do not inject AssistantToolExecutor into the command provider just to get helpers: exporting userPrincipal/agentPrincipal unchanged avoids reviving the existing proposer/executor late-binding dependency. The nine permission keys are comment.create, ticket.create, ticket.update, ticket.link.add, memory.create, memory.decision.record, fleet.job.dispatch, fleet.job.cancel and fleet.job.requeue; do not register read tools or invent a parallel dispatcher.

ApprovalGate.gate already resolves subjects from currentContext, parses input, resolves policy, and either executes under an approval context or opens a request (apps/api/src/approvals/approval-gate.service.ts:39-95). SYSTEM/assistant with onBehalfOf maps to ASSISTANT; USER/AGENT actors use their own subjects. The resolver already defaults ASSISTANT to human and otherwise uses catalog defaults; ASSISTANT policies do not inherit principal role matches (apps/api/src/approvals/approval-policy.resolver.ts:19,30-59,64-71). It is provided but not exported by ApprovalEngineModule (apps/api/src/approvals/approval-engine.module.ts:24-34); US-005 exports the existing provider, not a new resolver instance. The gate's duplicate match is actor/on-behalf-of/key/project/frozen-input hash, with live pending expiry filtering; it is not protected by a unique index (apps/api/src/approvals/approval-gate.service.ts:98-141; apps/api/src/approvals/prisma-approval-request.repository.ts:79). Including jobId in command input intentionally separates identical writes in different turns. Do not add a new deduplication contract or replace the gate's existing one.

Execution and actor attribution: the current executor already opens SYSTEM/assistant on behalf of the job's requester for a thread and the calling principal's own mcp context for MCP (apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/assistant-tool.executor.ts:196-231). Preserve these contexts, the replay mutex, the (jobId, toolCallId) stored-response behavior, permission-before-preview checks, explicit project resolution for WORKSPACE/MCP, and the separate AssistantToolCall ledger (same file:177-189,235-251,275-335,464-476). writeTool currently calls approvalModeFor and requires ActionProposer before preview (same file:362-411); proposeWrite accepts users only and directWrite records a PendingAction with an action-id suffix (same file:415-461). US-005 replaces waiting thread writes, US-006 replaces direct thread writes, and US-009 replaces MCP writes before US-011 deletes the obsolete branches. That staging is intentional; do not delete ActionProposer or MCP's old read in US-005. userPrincipal and agentPrincipal are module-private helpers to export unchanged (same file:570-607). AssistantToolCallRepository currently exposes only findUserActor, findByCall, record and findCallContext (apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/assistant-tool-call.domain.ts:64-71). Add findAgentActor and findProjectSlug to the interface, its Prisma implementation and every typed test double. findUserActor derives global role from role bindings, not User.role (apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/prisma-assistant-tool-call.repository.ts:81-94). Its existing requester helper already loads agent id/slug/status (same file:125-135); reuse the shape without changing requester attribution. The new project lookup must exclude soft-deleted projects.

Command contract and security: freeze only { projectId, threadId, jobId, args }, not preview, tool name or a serialized principal. The engine owns approval metadata; the command reconstructs its ToolContext from the action context, fresh actor data and project membership. Load the on-behalf-of principal only for SYSTEM/assistant; otherwise use the USER/AGENT actor. Refuse missing principals, disabled users, PAUSED agents and denied membership. Resolve the project slug afresh; use fresh time/fence and PermissionService.can scoped to the action project. ToolContext and error classes are defined at apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/assistant-tool.types.ts:16-49,64-91. Success text is masked and byte-capped at RESULT_CAP_BYTES (16,384; apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/assistant-tool.executor.ts:23). Every command error must propagate unchanged. ApprovalExecutionService already performs input-hash, command, parse and stillHoldsKey prechecks, executes inside a settle transaction, rolls back command failures and settles failed in a separate transaction with { error: 'execution-failed', name } (apps/api/src/approvals/approval-execution.service.ts:45-98,104-170). This differs deliberately from today's executeAction, which catches tool errors and returns partial text. Approved batches become atomic; direct batches retain already committed partial effects and masked ToolActionError text. Never catch a nested transaction failure inside the command: SEC-16 invalidates the outer transaction. Direct calls must not acquire a thread lock or an outer transaction, both to retain partial-write behavior and to avoid inversion with fleet job-then-thread locks. A policy can change between pre-resolution and gate resolution: waiting-to-none may execute inside the waiting transaction; none-to-waiting creates a link without the normal cap. These are specified exceptions, not reasons to hold locks on every write.

Persistence and lifecycle: PendingAction currently owns duplicated approval state and nullable thread/job/call provenance (apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma:1113-1146), and ChatThread has pendingActions at schema.prisma:1218. ApprovalRequest already owns actor/on-behalf-of, frozen input, requiredMode, approver, result, expiry and lowercase statuses (schema.prisma:1621-1668). US-001 adds AssistantActionRequest, keyed by requestId, with only thread provenance/preview/note/delivery marks; add both relation fields and migration 20261105090000_assistant_action_request. Both link foreign keys cascade when their parent is deleted, but deleting a thread must delete only links, not ApprovalRequest. jobId, toolCallId and note/delivery message ids remain bookkeeping strings, not additional foreign keys. The new repository follows AbstractPrismaRepository with all four mappers and a private DI symbol (.nax/rules/api-repositories.md:12-51). Use generated Prisma client types, never @prisma/client, with transaction-scoped PrismaService access. Existing lockThread and insertSystemNote are the exact patterns to retain (apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/actions/prisma-pending-action.repository.ts:81-85,175-179). allocateThreadSeq already handles nextSeq lagging older messages and requires the caller's thread lock (apps/api/src/fleet/threads/domain/chat-thread.domain.ts:34-40). Waiting writes lock thread, then count pending links before calling the gate's duplicate lookup, then insert one missing link inside bookkeeping('assistant.action-request-link'). A new link gets one post-commit thread frame. The cap stays 10. A repeated toolCallId remains an executor replay; a different toolCallId with identical parsed input uses the gate duplicate while below the cap.

Reads and delivery dependencies: koda_get_action currently depends on two PendingAction scope queries and renders uppercase status/string result (apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/tools/action-tools.ts:84-111). US-005 changes thread reads to request-plus-link while temporarily retaining the MCP repository dependency; US-009 changes MCP to findOwnRequest for AGENT actor/project and removes the old injection. Render lowercase statuses, requested/optional decided/optional settled lines, and fence only a present result.text. For unlinked MCP requests use permissionKey instead of a tool display name. Scope filters must be part of the query: another thread/project/agent gets the same not_found as a missing id. PrismaChatThreadRepository.pendingActions currently filters via scopeWhere and sorts oldest-first with the cap, then reads each action's own project slug (apps/api/src/fleet/threads/prisma-chat-thread.repository.ts:131-148). Preserve that WORKSPACE security fence when switching to linked pending requests in US-007. Its id and approvalId must both become the request id; keep PendingActionDto shape and its existing description. Current outcome delivery reads PendingAction and marks only the first byte-fitting notes on the new message (same file:429-445); job assignment rebuilds from deliveredMessageId, not stored transcript notes (apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/prisma-fleet-job.repository.ts:256-265). Move both reads together in US-004 so send and every assignment/requeue rebuild exactly the same content. Keep deliveryText's byte cap and MAX_DELIVERED_NOTES=20; only the deliverable statuses change to executed, failed, rejected, expired, cancelled (apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/actions/outcome-delivery.ts:2-32). Delivery derives from settled requests even if the asynchronous transcript note has not yet arrived.

Outbox notes: ApprovalRequestEvents already records a content-free approval_request_changed payload in the status transaction; subscribers load result from queries instead of event payload (apps/api/src/approvals/approval-request-events.ts:6-65). ApprovalRequestQueries.findById is an unscoped system-reader seam (apps/api/src/approvals/approval-request.queries.ts:43-46). Mirror onModuleInit registration and malformed-payload warning from apps/api/src/live/approval-request-live.subscriber.ts:13-25, and the writing-subscriber pattern at apps/api/src/notifications/approvals/approval-requested.subscriber.ts:12-36. Do not copy the live subscriber's catch-all best-effort error swallowing: DB errors in the new note writer must reach the relay so it retries. FanOutPublisher runs every handler inside runAsSystem('outbox') and retries all handlers after any aggregate failure (apps/api/src/outbox/fan-out-publisher.ts:23-34,70-93). Declare @SystemWriter('system.thread.ingest') but do not call runAsSystemWriter. Under one transaction lock thread then link, check notedAt, re-read request, allocate/insert note and markNoted; only after commit publish message then thread frames. Ignore nonterminal statuses, missing links, null thread ids and deleted threads. Transcript note text must come from requestOutcomeNote, including generic failures except NotFoundAppException and a 500-character-plus-ellipsis result cap. Keep note bookkeeping separate from delivery bookkeeping. System-writer expectations go 36 -> 37 in US-003 and back to 36 after deleting PendingActionExpirySweeper in US-011 (apps/api/src/permissions/system-writer.decorator.spec.ts:46,103).

Decision route and compatibility: use the existing POST /approvals/:id/decisions route; the controller checks visibility and delegates to ApprovalDecisionService (apps/api/src/approvals/approval-requests.controller.ts:67-88). Do not add a thread-specific decide endpoint. decideEligibility refuses nonprincipals, checks own/on-behalf-of permissions, scoped decide grants and mode tier in order; on-behalf-of contributes human even for an agent requester (apps/api/src/approvals/approval-eligibility.ts:48-107). The requester may decide without a separate approval.decide grant when still holding the action, while Project Admins and other eligible deciders may decide with the engine's permissions. Revoked action permission yields 403 approvals.decideForbidden/missing-action-permission and preserves pending status. Preserve requester authorship when a different admin approves. Expiry uses the existing engine sweeper, whose tick is public but whose provider is intentionally not exported (apps/api/src/approvals/approval-request-expiry.sweeper.ts:16-35,77-79; approval-engine.module.ts:21). Resolve it in integration tests using app.get(ApprovalRequestExpirySweeper, { strict: false }). Outcome notes appear after relay dispatch, not synchronously with decisions.

Web seam: ThreadActionCard currently imports useFleetApprovals and posts action.approvalId with a fleet body, while preserving a local decided flag, in-flight disabling, countdown and API-error toast (apps/web/components/fleet/threads/ThreadActionCard.vue:4,25-49). useFleetApprovals is tied to project/admin fleet routes and mutation counters (apps/web/composables/useFleetApprovals.ts:7-11,43-49); do not repurpose it or delete the fleet inbox. Post { decision } plus non-empty comment to /approvals/<id>/decisions and switch the card to action.id, with no call to useFleetApprovals.
